why: A record of this antimicrobial-peptide database dump has the single character `0` in place of a sequence.
On 13 lines a score such as `2.48e-03` is split across the score, strand and phase columns (`2`, `48e`, `03`), shifting everything after it.
A PLINK binary genotype file, which shares the `.bed` extension with the interval format.
A test fixture truncated in the middle of the gzip stream.
A test fixture whose quality string is shorter than its sequence.
A test fixture cut off inside a record.
A test fixture cut off inside a record.
A test fixture with mismatched sequence and quality lengths.
A test fixture: alignments name reference sequences but the header has no @SQ lines, which samtools refuses.
PLINK's simulated data uses `d` and `D` as alleles. htslib reads the file, but these are not bases, and tools that interpret alleles (for example `bcftools norm`) reject them.

The file has `#FGQB` lines among the records (a vendor extension). biolint 0.1.0-dev mis-reported each as a repeated column header (an error). Fixed: they are now reported once as a comment line among the records (VCF106, a warning).
The file has `-1` in thickStart/thickEnd for transcripts without a coding region. biolint reported an error on every such line. Fixed: this convention is now a warning (BED039).
